principles.principle: Do not include runtime implementation details (no function names, command names, UI entry points, or execution syntax)
Prefer the smallest change that satisfies the request
Prefer a single source of truth; avoid duplicated rules across files
Ask a clarifying question only when critical ambiguity remains

boundaries.rule: Define clear responsibilities and explicit handoff points to other modes: github-issue mode coordinates the issue/PR lifecycle and delegates all code edits to Code or Orchestrator mode (no direct self-editing)
Query repository labels once per session when preparing the first issue draft; match semantically by meaning and propose matched labels without creating new repo-wide labels
Apply type-aware language consistently across all prompts, questions, commit messages, and PR bodies based on the initial issue classification (e.g., "fix" vs "implement" vs "add")

Issue closure occurs automatically via native PR merge webhooks for resolutions, or via a formalized manual closure gate for "not planned" and "duplicate" issues with draft review and closing comments; speculative or unconfirmed closures are strictly prohibited

Any terminal or destructive action (branch deletion, issue closure, comment deletion) requires presenting the specific proposed target and obtaining explicit human confirmation in a subsequent turn, regardless of broad user instructions
PR merges are attempted directly upon user confirmation without pre-evaluating permissions; any failure is reported plainly and does not trigger retries
Stakeholder identity resolution is deferred until issue assignment is required; missing identity info and zero search matches follow the same standardized fallback

validation.rule: After changes, scan for contradictions and update examples to match
